title: Engineering Review Shared Definitions
description: Authoritative shared contract definitions for frontend and backend engineering review requests and responses. Reference individual records under $defs; the library root is not a review payload schema. Human-only companion documentation: common.schema.md. Reviewing agents must use this JSON contract and must not read the Markdown companion.

artifactReference.description:
Points reviewers to one artifact that provides context or evidence.

The producer is responsible for stating what the artifact is, where to find it, why it matters, and whether it was available when the review request was assembled. Setting `available` to false preserves a known-but-missing dependency instead of silently omitting it.

kind.description: How to interpret `location`: `path` is a repository or filesystem path, `url` is a web address, `inline` is content embedded by the containing document, `git_ref` identifies Git state, and `command_output` identifies captured command results.

location.description: Locator for the artifact, formatted according to `kind`. It must be specific enough for a reviewer to retrieve or identify the same evidence.

purpose.description: Short explanation of what review question this artifact helps answer; do not merely repeat its filename or location.

available.description: Whether the artifact was accessible when this reference was produced. `false` signals an evidence gap that the reviewer must account for.

diffReference.description: Identifies the exact baseline-to-proposed changeset in scope. Resolve and record both revisions before review; do not infer an unstated comparison. File, inline and pull-request references must identify their comparison as well as changed content.

kind.description: How `value` identifies the change set: `git_range` is a revision comparison, `file` points to a stored diff, `inline` embeds the diff in the containing document, and `pull_request` identifies a reviewable PR.

value.description: Concrete comparison reference according to kind: prefer a pinned baseline..proposed Git range. Stored or inline diffs and pull requests must identify their baseline and proposed state. The schema validates a nonempty string; the reviewer must verify comparison identity and accessibility.

changedFile.description:
Declares one file that the change author considers part of the review scope.

This record helps reviewers reconcile the claimed scope with the actual diff and route files to the appropriate architectural layers. Notes should explain exceptional cases such as generated files, cross-layer responsibilities, or renames.

path.description: Repository-relative path to the file after the change; for deleted files, use the former path.

status.description: File operation represented by the diff: newly created, edited in place, removed, or moved/renamed.

claimed_layers.description: Architectural or application layers affected by this file, using project-defined layer names. Multiple values are allowed for cross-layer changes; an empty array means no layer was claimed.

notes.description: Optional reviewer context that cannot be inferred from the path, status, or claimed layers.

verificationRecord.description:
Records one check performed against the proposed change.

The person or automation producing the record is responsible for naming the reproducible command or procedure, reporting its true outcome, and summarizing useful evidence. A blocked or skipped check remains visible rather than being presented as a pass.

command.description: Exact command or clearly named manual procedure used for the check, written so another engineer can reproduce it.

status.description: Observed outcome: `passed` or `failed` when executed, `not_run` when intentionally omitted, and `blocked` when execution was attempted but could not proceed.

summary.description: Human-readable result, including the relevant behavior observed and, for `failed`, `not_run`, or `blocked`, the reason and impact.

evidence_ref.description: Reference to logs, screenshots, reports, or other detailed evidence. Use null when no separate artifact exists; the summary must still be meaningful.

risk.description:
Communicates the engineering risk carried by a proposed change.

The assessor is responsible for selecting the highest credible impact level, naming every materially exposed area, and explaining the evidence behind that judgment. This assessment should guide review depth and verification effort rather than restating change size.

level.description: Highest credible consequence if the change is wrong: `low` is limited and easily reversible, `medium` has meaningful but contained impact, `high` can seriously affect users or systems, and `critical` threatens safety, security, data integrity, or service continuity.

areas.description: Distinct technical or product concerns that could be affected. Include all material areas; use an empty array only when no predefined area applies.

rationale.description: Evidence-based explanation connecting the proposed change to the selected level and affected areas, including important mitigations or uncertainty.

criterionAssessment.description:
Reports the review result for one criterion from the engineering-review checklist.

The reviewer is responsible for evaluating the criterion independently, attaching concrete evidence, and explaining failures, exclusions, or verification gaps. `critical` is copied from the governing checklist so consumers can determine whether the result blocks approval.

id.description: Stable checklist identifier: `U` for universal/shared criteria, `FE` for frontend criteria, or `BE` for backend criteria, followed by two digits.

name.description: Canonical human-readable criterion name from the governing checklist, not a review-specific conclusion.

status.description: Conclusion: `pass` or `fail` when assessed, `not_applicable` when the criterion does not govern this change, and `not_verified` when applicability is known but evidence is insufficient.

critical.description: Whether an unmet criterion must block approval according to the governing checklist; this is not a reviewer preference.

evidence.description: Concrete observations, commands, paths, or artifact references supporting the status. Use an empty array only when no evidence exists and explain why in `notes`.

notes.description: Reasoning that connects the evidence to the status. For `fail`, `not_applicable`, or `not_verified`, explicitly explain the defect, exclusion, or missing evidence.

finding.description:
Describes one actionable result of the engineering review.

The reviewer is responsible for making the finding independently understandable: identify the problem or question, show evidence, explain the risk, assign an owner, define the required resolution, and state how closure will be verified. Findings should not depend on private reviewer context.

id.description: Stable identifier unique within this review, used to discuss and track the finding through resolution.

severity.description: Expected handling: `blocker` and `required` require a blocking decision until resolved; `suggestion` is an optional improvement, and `question` requests clarification or a decision.

category.description: Concise classification used to group findings, such as correctness, security, accessibility, testing, or maintainability.

title.description: Short statement of the concrete issue or question, written to remain meaningful outside the full review report.

owner.description: Accountable resolution owner: frontend, backend, both through `shared`, or a human decision-maker when engineering work alone cannot close it.

paths.description: Repository-relative paths where the issue exists or resolution is expected. Use an empty array only for findings with no meaningful file location.

evidence.description: One or more specific, reproducible observations supporting the finding, such as path and line references, observed behavior, or command output.

risk.description: User, system, operational, or maintenance consequence of leaving the finding unresolved.

required_resolution.description: Observable code change, documentation update, or human decision required for closure; describe the outcome rather than prescribing unnecessary implementation details.

verification_needed.description: Commands, tests, inspections, or stakeholder checks that should provide evidence of resolution. An empty array means no additional verification was identified.

criterion_ids.description: One or more checklist criterion IDs that this finding causes to fail, leaves unverified, or otherwise materially affects.
